notes: Footage from a phone is read the way you see it. A portrait iPhone clip is stored sideways with a rotation flag, and Crisp was reading the stored shape — so it told you a vertical video was “already widescreen” and quietly re-encoded it when you asked to make it vertical. Anamorphic footage was wrong the other way. Asking for a ratio as a decimal works too: “make it 1.91:1” used to plan a square. A width on a watermark (“add a watermark 200px wide”) now sizes the watermark instead of being mistaken for shrinking the video. And “stabilise it” measures your clip first — on a tripod shot or a smooth pan it says so rather than adding wobble.
